teaches: A dialogue two-shot built as an escalation machine: locked camera, one living-room background, and two stock puppets on separate scene layers trading grief beats for 209 frames. Gumball leads — teary and wobbling from f1, open-mouthed wail at f27, collapsed to his knees sobbing by f131 — and Darwin answers each beat late (flat until f53, tear streaks at f79, his own floor collapse at f183) until both end bawling on the floor at f209. The face system does nearly all of it: GB_HEADCOMP alone holds 1,190 keyframes, the largest symbol in the file, and face comps total 4,699 kf against 1,505 body-puppet kf.
notes: Offset timing is the structure: Darwin's beats land roughly 25-50 frames after Gumball's matching beat — his tear streaks appear at f79 after Gumball's open wail at f27, his floor collapse at f183 after Gumball's at f131.
The collapses are staged by body position on the same stock puppets (standing, then kneeling, then slumped sitting) — no special 'crying' puppet variants exist in the file.
Tears are face-comp elements: white tear streaks on the head comps from f79 onward, growing with the performance.
Render needed repeated FFDec attempts under cross-batch contention (cached counts 147, then 185, then 204) before an attempt completed the full 209/209.
